title: Special Relativity: Time Dilation and E = mc²
seo_title: Year 12 Physics: Special Relativity Worksheets (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Inertial frames and Einstein's postulates; the constant speed of light; relativity of simultaneity; time dilation and length contraction; evidence from muons, GPS and particle accelerators; relativistic momentum and mass–energy equivalence. (Senior Secondary Physics, Unit 4: Revolutions in modern physics)
meta_desc: Free Year 12 Physics worksheets on special relativity: Einstein's postulates, the Lorentz factor, time dilation, length contraction, muons, GPS, relativistic momentum and E = mc². 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: t = γt₀; L = L₀ ÷ γ; E = mc².
body_html:
How to think about it

Einstein's postulates: the laws of physics are the same in all inertial frames, and the speed of light is the same for every observer. As a result, a moving clock runs slow (time dilation, t = γt₀) and a moving object is shorter along its motion (length contraction, L = L₀/γ).

γ is close to 1 at everyday speeds but grows without limit as v approaches c, so no object with mass can reach light speed. Muons reaching the ground and GPS clock corrections confirm relativity. Mass and energy are equivalent: E = mc².

Example

γ at 0.8c?

1 − 0.64 = 0.36

√0.36 = 0.6

1 ÷ 0.6

Answer: 1.67

Example

At 0.8c a 2.0 s tick (on board) seen from Earth?

t = γt₀ = 1.67 × 2.0

Answer: 3.33 s

Common mistakes

  • Applying length contraction at right angles to the motion.
  • Mixing up proper time and dilated time.
  • Thinking the speed of light changes for a moving observer.

faq.q: Is time dilation real or an illusion?
faq.a: It is real and measured: fast-moving muons live longer in our frame, and clocks flown on aircraft and satellites run at measurably different rates.

faq.q: Why can't we notice relativity in daily life?
faq.a: At everyday speeds γ is extremely close to 1, so the effects are far too small to see.

items.q: A spacecraft moves at 0.6c relative to Earth. On board, the interval between two ticks of a clock lasts 60 s. How long does it last as measured from Earth?
items.e: Moving clocks run slow: t = γt₀ = 1.25 × 60 = 75 s.

items.q: Calculate the relativistic momentum of a proton (mass 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg) moving at 0.75c.

c: the observer sees it run slow (time dilation)
items.e: t = γt₀.

Why do muons made high in the atmosphere reach Earth's surface?
c: their lifetime is dilated in Earth's frame (or the distance is contracted in theirs)
items.e: This is direct evidence for time dilation.

items.q: Calculate the relativistic momentum of a proton (mass 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg) moving at 0.995c.
Why must GPS satellites correct their clocks for relativity?
c: the speed of light changes in space
their clocks run at a different rate from clocks on the ground because of their speed and weaker gravity
items.e: Without corrections, positions would drift by kilometres a day.

items.q: What is proper length?
c: the length of an object measured in its own rest frame
the length of a light year
the length seen by a moving observer
the length after it is heated
items.e: Moving observers measure a shorter length.

items.q: A spacecraft moves at 0.75c relative to Earth. On board, an experiment lasts 15 min. How long does it last as measured from Earth?

items.q: Observers on Earth measure the journey on a spacecraft moving at 0.995c as 20 years. What is the proper time measured on board?
items.e: Proper time t₀ = t ÷ γ = 20 ÷ 10 = 2 years.

items.q: Calculate the Lorentz factor γ for a speed of 0.98c.
Why can no object with mass reach the speed of light?
c: its relativistic momentum and energy would become infinite
it would lose all its mass
items.e: Particle accelerators get very close but never reach c.

items.q: What are the two postulates of special relativity?
c: time is absolute and space is absolute
mass is always conserved and energy is not
the laws of physics are the same in all inertial frames, and the speed of light in a vacuum is the same for all observers
items.e: Einstein, 1905.

What is an inertial frame of reference?
c: a frame moving faster than light
any frame on Earth's surface accelerating upwards
a frame that is not accelerating
items.e: Newton's first law holds in it.

items.q: What did the Michelson–Morley experiment show?
c: that the speed of light changes with direction
no evidence of an 'aether', supporting a constant speed of light
items.e: It found no change in light speed with Earth's motion.

items.q: What is proper time?
c: the time on a clock in a moving frame seen from outside
the time it takes light to travel 1 m
the time between two events measured by an observer for whom they happen at the same place
items.e: Proper time is the shortest measured time.
